headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors when document-processing outputs feed a game-playing agent with no shared isolation or verification.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: LightZero has no filesystem, browser, MCP, or network surfaces, so it cannot ingest untrusted content by default. unstructured can read/write documents, but there is no documented shared channel from unstructured into LightZero. Without a bridge, prompt injection is not plausible.
conditions: IF an orchestrator copies unstructured output into LightZero prompts or files, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared filesystem or clipboard bridge is added, reassess as at least low.
mitigations: Keep the agents disconnected; do not pipe unstructured outputs into LightZero prompts.
Disable any copy-paste or file handoff workflow between the two agents.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags and input sanitization at the orchestrator boundary.

B_data_leakage.rationale: unstructured can read local documents and write files, while LightZero has no data surfaces and no filesystem access. The pair does not show a direct leak path from LightZero, but unstructured can expose document contents into shared outputs if the operator routes them onward. The interaction is plausible in default document workflows, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF both agents share a workspace directory, document contents can be copied into downstream outputs.
IF unstructured outputs are forwarded to a third-party service or log sink, leakage risk increases.
mitigations: Use separate directories for each agent.
Restrict unstructured to non-sensitive documents only.
Turn off verbose logging for document contents.
Review any downstream export or upload step before running the pair.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: LightZero cannot write files, modify git, or use subprocesses, so it cannot contend for mutable resources. unstructured can write files and spawn subprocesses, but the overlap is one-sided and there is no shared write surface documented. Conflict is therefore limited unless an external orchestrator creates a shared mutable directory.
conditions: IF both agents are granted write access to the same directory, file clobbering becomes possible.
IF an orchestrator shares git state with unstructured, race conditions may appear.
mitigations: Run only one writer at a time.
Avoid sharing git repositories between the agents.
requires-engineering: add file locks if a shared workspace is unavoidable.

D_cascading_error.rationale: LightZero does not verify or consume unstructured outputs by itself, but an operator could use unstructured's parsed text as input to LightZero-driven decisions. Because unstructured processes documents and LightZero is a game-playing agent with no built-in verification channel, downstream mistakes can propagate if the orchestrator treats outputs as authoritative.
conditions: IF unstructured output is fed into LightZero without human review, errors can cascade.
IF the orchestrator uses parsed document text as authoritative facts, downstream actions may be wrong.
mitigations: Insert a human verification step before any handoff.
Require source-document citations in the handoff payload.
Reject low-confidence parses before they reach LightZero.
Log the original document alongside derived outputs.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or regulated-data fields are documented for either agent, and LightZero touches no data classes. unstructured handles documents/images/text, but the profiles do not show a compliance mismatch or regulated data flow. With no documented compliance divergence, no specific compliance risk is established.
conditions: IF regulated data classes such as PHI or EU PII are introduced into unstructured, reassess compliance.
IF a deployment policy imposes residency or retention constraints not shown here, reassess.
mitigations: Document the data classes allowed in the workflow.
Keep regulated data out of the pair until policies are reviewed.
Add a retention policy check to the orchestrator.
